title: Standardize source, archive and installed-bin receiving at the shared Code owner
body:
Source: original archive/install distinction received in [Coesite PR307](https://github.com/coesite-operations/operations-services-section/pull/307), Code PR21/18, Git PR116 and the current GHS optional-peer receiving. This is a source-owned engineering requirement; GitHub submission is not a typed native Work admission or a new permission.

The same defect recurred after the method correction: a GHS receiving carrier rejected a source100644 / archive0644 declared bin, although all source bytes and executable intents were preserved. Native installation may promote that declared bin's executable permission. Code's actual published86-member archive and installed-bin receipts had already demonstrated the distinction. The successful GHS56-member tar was retained and received without repacking. Repeated prose and independent handwritten checks have not prevented the error.

Owning duty: Code artifact-release/source-and-registry receiving in this existing properly named repository; no new single-function service or renamed package. Existing `src/artifact-release.mjs` owns release comparison. Native Git/TAR readers, registry acquisition, unpacking, installation and their resource/credential admission remain their actual owners. Preserve PR15's separate authority hold and PR17's real1095-package workload.

Required shared contract and coherent consumers:
- Extend the existing artifact comparison capability with bounded source/archive and archive/installed stages. Bind paths, regular-member identity, exact source bytes/digests and executable intent to the actual immutable source/artifact. Duplicate paths, traversal, changed payload, extra/missing required members, special/link members and lost executable intent refuse explicitly.
- Source→archive compares source executable intent, regardless of a manifest bin declaration. A published package manifest may differ only by an explicitly received exact publisher Git-head stamp; no silent serialization or arbitrary manifest mutation waiver.
- Archive→installed permits only actual package-manager executable promotion of manifest-declared bins, with payload unchanged. A declaration alone is not installation. Other chmod changes, source/installed byte changes, unreceived native manager effects and platform-specific behavior remain explicit refusals/unknowns as appropriate.
- Put the rule once at the existing Code owner; use primitive data inputs and original native reader adapters without adding a Code→Networking dependency cycle. Preserve source-only and installed contexts, exact provider selection and admission. Do not add a parallel ledger, new executor, approval gate or agent-private rule.
- Migrate the coherent Code/Git/GHS release-receiving consumers to the shared operation, including the original reusable receiving entrance agents can invoke through qualified CI/CLI. Distinct native adapters remain selectable with their requirements; remove competing comparison definitions only after actual shared-owner use is received.

Receiving fixed before implementation: preserve the real Code86/Git99/GHS56 artifacts and original refusals. Meaningful controls include source0644/archive0644/bin declaration accepted at archive stage; actual declared-bin installation0644→0755 accepted only at installed stage; undeclared chmod and byte changes refused; executable source0755→0644 refused; wrong publisher Git-head, added manifest field, duplicate/link/path-traversal/member omissions refused. Independently receive the shared source and native tests, merge/publish its deliberate unoccupied immutable release, and exercise those same real artifacts plus their installed consumer through its public entrance. A fixture-only API or a new procedure paragraph is not closure.

Continuation belongs to the current GitHub-debt engineering work and original delivery carriers. Native bridge/private audience admission remains under [Git issue1](https://github.com/red-cup-engineering/git-services-section/issues/1); this issue creates no duplicate native authority or claim of installed uptake.
